plan_a_advantages: Includes a dedicated tempo run for speed development.
Longer runs (18km) better mimic race distances and build trail endurance.
Consistent moderate pace focus supports overall speed improvement.
plan_b_advantages: Stronger emphasis on strength and mobility training.
More clearly defined intensity targets (easy, steady, controlled, threshold).
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a dedicated tempo run (11km at controlled pace) which directly addresses the need for increased speed and lactate threshold – a key component of trail running performance. Plan B, while well-structured, lacks this focused speed work, relying primarily on easy runs and a single tempo session. Plan A’s longer runs (18km) also better simulate the demands of trail races, building endurance and trail-specific adaptations. Furthermore, the consistent 'moderate pace' focus in Plan A aligns with the goal of improving overall speed, whereas Plan B’s emphasis on 'controlled effort' could potentially hinder the athlete from pushing themselves to faster paces.
